Green Light Studio · Press Kit Alpha v0.2 · 28 Aug 2026

“You are not a soldier. You are the commander.”

1944 Eastern Front · Commander-perspective RTS · PC / Android

01 Overview

Build a company from the Wehrmacht or the Red Army, commit it to a three-lane front, and break the enemy headquarters — or out-hold them on victory points when the clock runs out.

SPEARHEAD strips away unit micromanagement. You command squads and vehicles, not individual soldiers. What you decide is what to field, where to send it, and when — and that is the whole game. Matches run ten to fifteen minutes, so a decision is rewarded or punished quickly.

Tank combat has no health bars. Every shot resolves as real penetration: plate thickness, slope, impact angle, range. A round that gets through does not subtract a number — it breaks a track, kills the engine, jams the turret, or sets off the ammunition. A T-34 that reaches a Tiger's flank wins that exchange. Angle beats statistics.

03 Key Features

  1. MACRO

    Command, don't babysit

    Combat units advance on their own; the only way back is a retreat order. Your attention goes to composition, timing and ground — not to keeping twelve squads alive by hand.

  2. ARMOR

    Penetration, not hit points

    Shots are traced against hull and turret colliders, resolved by face, angle and range. Crews bail out, wrecks can be recovered for manpower, and damaged vehicles can be repaired in the field.

  3. ACE

    Two seats, one battle

    While one player runs the front, another can crew a single tank and aim it themselves — sights, ammunition, reload. The ace fires under the same penetration rules as everything else. On mobile, the tank seat is the whole game.

  4. 1944

    History as rules, not decoration

    Real 1944 organisation and weapon data drive the simulation — magazine capacity, cyclic rate, muzzle velocity. German quality against Soviet quantity is the balance, not something corrected away. No swastikas are used.
